assumptions.chosen: Each cell shows the value as recorded on the run (purpose e.g. "build", worker e.g. "claude-code", task class e.g. "build", reason = the recorded route reason text, task key e.g. "T3"); a purpose may additionally be followed by a human label. The context size is the recorded byte count as an integer (digit grouping and a trailing "bytes"/"B" unit allowed); when no context package was recorded the cell shows "—", like the audit log's empty Task cell. Newest first = by run start time, latest first. A run with no recorded worker/task class/reason (older runs) shows "—" in that cell.
assumptions.question: How are the purpose, worker, task class, reason and context size written in the "Recent worker runs" table, and in what order are runs "newest first"?

assumptions.chosen: The Router's decision for a standard-tier task with all enabled workers available, computed from the recorded qualification records at the time the page is opened; Worker and Reason are exactly the Router's chosen worker id and reason text. An alternative's status is "disabled" when the worker is not enabled in the Router's table, otherwise the Router's qualification status; its samples are the number of recorded qualification samples the Router counts for that worker and class.
assumptions.question: Which worker "would run that class now", given that the Router's decision also depends on the task's risk tier and on quota pauses?

assumptions.chosen: Like the other preview demo data (APP_ENV=preview only), two finished demo runs: first a run on demo task T1 with purpose "draft_contract", worker "claude-code", task class "contract_draft", reason "trusted worker (no alternative is defined for this class)" and no context package; then, started later, a run on demo task T3 with purpose "build", worker "claude-code", task class "build", reason "trusted worker (no alternative has qualified for this class)" and a context package of 48213 bytes. Plus three demo qualification records for worker "local-llm", task class "log_summary", mode shadow, valid and agreeing. No other qualification records.
assumptions.question: What demonstration data does the gate preview carry for these sections?

interface.ui: Sign-in for the gate preview: GET /auth/preview (redirects to / with an owner session). System page: route /system (navigation link "System"), page title "System · Agents", h1 "System" (unchanged). NEW section 1: a card with heading (h2) exactly "Recent worker runs" on /system, containing a table whose column headers are, in this order: "Task", "Purpose", "Worker", "Task class", "Reason", "Context bytes". One body row per worker run, at most 20, newest first (by start time). Task cell: the task key (preview: "T1", "T3"; it may link to /tasks/{id}). Purpose cell: the recorded purpose (preview: "build", "draft_contract"), optionally followed by a human label. Worker cell: the recorded worker id (preview: "claude-code"). Task class cell: the recorded task class (preview: "build", "contract_draft"). Reason cell: the recorded route reason (preview: "trusted worker (no alternative has qualified for this class)", "trusted worker (no alternative is defined for this class)"). Context bytes cell: the recorded byte count as an integer (preview: 48213; digit grouping such as "48,213" and a trailing "bytes" or "B" are allowed), or exactly "—" (U+2014) when the run had no context package; any other unrecorded value is also shown as "—". With no runs, the section shows the text "No worker runs yet" and no table body rows. Preview rows, top to bottom: [T3 | build | claude-code | build | trusted worker (no alternative has qualified for this class) | 48213], [T1 | draft_contract | claude-code | contract_draft | trusted worker (no alternative is defined for this class) | —]. NEW section 2: a card with heading (h2) exactly "Routing and qualification" on /system, containing a table whose column headers are, in this order: "Task class", "Worker", "Reason", "Alternatives". Exactly one body row per Router task class, in the Router's order: contract_draft, plan, build, correction, mutants, check_author, acceptance_check, attribution, failure_triage, log_summary (Task class cell shows that identifier). Worker cell: the worker id the Router would choose now for a standard-tier task; Reason cell: the Router's reason text. Alternatives cell: for each alternative worker the Router defines for that class, in the Router's order, one entry (e.g. a list item or line) containing the worker id, its status as exactly one of the words "unqualified", "shadow", "qualified", "rejected", "disabled", and its sample count written as "{n} samples" (e.g. "codex-builder disabled 0 samples"); exactly "—" when the class has no alternative. Preview values (A3 demo data): build and correction: Worker "claude-code", Reason "trusted worker (no alternative has qualified for this class)", alternatives codex-builder disabled 0 samples, opencode-local disabled 0 samples; failure_triage: Worker "codex-verifier", Reason "trusted worker (no alternative has qualified for this class)", alternative local-llm unqualified 0 samples; log_summary: Worker "claude-code", Reason "trusted worker (no alternative has qualified for this class)", alternative local-llm shadow 3 samples; contract_draft, plan, mutants: Worker "claude-code"; check_author, acceptance_check, attribution: Worker "codex-verifier"; all six with Reason "trusted worker (no alternative is defined for this class)" and Alternatives "—". Existing content on /system keeps its headings: "Backups", "Recent executor errors", "Administrative operations (audit log)"; tiles "Build" and "Executor jobs".

non_goals: Showing other ledger fields (harness, model, provider, permission envelope, context file list, extra files, failure class, status, outcome, duration, cost) - they may be shown but are not required.
Filtering, sorting, searching or paginating either table; showing more than the 20 most recent runs; any per-run detail page.
Changing the Router (src/domain/router.ts): its rule table, workers, qualification thresholds or how it decides; changing how runs or qualification records are recorded.
Enabling, disabling, qualifying or rejecting a worker, or recording qualification evidence, from the UI; any new button, form, action or API under /api/v0.
Showing the ledger or routing on other pages (Command page, project pages, task pages) or changing the task page's "Workers" card.
Estimates, projections, charts, progress indicators or animations of any kind.

Changing the existing System page content (heartbeat tiles, "Build", "Executor jobs", "Backups", "Recent executor errors", "Administrative operations (audit log)", any "Project Capabilities" section of other tasks) or its live refresh; changing sign-in, sessions or authorization.

scope.summary: The System page (/system) gains two independent, read-only sections. "Recent worker runs" is a table of the 20 most recent worker runs (newest first) showing, from the run records the control loop already writes, the task key, the run's purpose, the worker, the task class, the Router's reason for choosing that worker and the size of the context package in bytes (a dash when the run had none); with no runs it says "No worker runs yet". "Routing and qualification" is a table with one row per task class of the static Router showing the worker that would run that class now and the Router's reason, plus, for each alternative worker defined for that class, its qualification status (unqualified, shadow, qualified, rejected or disabled) and its number of recorded samples, derived from the recorded qualification evidence only. Nothing is estimated or animated. The gate preview's demonstration data gains demonstration worker runs (and a few demonstration qualification records) so both sections can be checked black-box. All other parts of the System page stay unchanged.
